questions.question: 79012. A high-copper amalgam alloy contains approximately:
questions.explain: The image classifies high-copper alloys as containing approximately 13–30% copper. They may be admixed or single-composition alloys.

questions.question: 79011. Which component is present in the highest percentage by weight in the GIC?
questions.explain:
Composition of GIC:
Silica (SiO₂) → 40.9%
Alumina (Al₂O₃) → 28.6%
Calcium fluoride (CaF₂) → 15.7%
Sodium fluoride (NaF) → 9.3%
Aluminum phosphate (AlPO₄) → 3.8%
Aluminum fluoride (AlF₃) → 1.6%

questions.question: 79010. Which impression material is most hydrophilic among the following?
questions.explain:
Polyether is relatively hydrophilic compared with many elastomeric impression materials.
This property helps it perform better in the presence of limited moisture.
However, excessive water absorption can affect its dimensional stability.
Proper moisture control is still necessary for accurate impressions

questions.question: 79009. Which dental cement has the greatest initial pulpal irritation?
questions.explain:
Zinc phosphate cement initially has a relatively low pH because of phosphoric acid.
Freshly mixed cement can therefore cause pulpal irritation, particularly in deep cavities.
Its acidity gradually decreases as the cement sets.
Adequate dentin thickness or an appropriate liner/base can provide pulpal protection

questions.question: 79008. Which appliance is specifically designed to modify the function of perioral muscles in growing patients?
questions.explain:
The Frankel appliance is a functional regulator.
It works primarily by influencing the surrounding muscles and soft tissues.
Its vestibular shields and lip pads alter the muscular environment around the dentition.
It is mainly used during growth for selected developing malocclusions

questions.question: 79007. The major advantage of zinc phosphate cement is its:
questions.explain: Zinc phosphate cement has good compressive strength, relatively low film thickness, and a long history of successful clinical use. However, it does not chemically bond to tooth structure.

questions.question: 79006. A central diastema is closed by applying a force from both sides toward the center. This is:
questions.explain:
The two central incisors are moved toward one another.
Both teeth experience forces of equal magnitude in opposite directions.
Since both anchorage units participate in the movement, it is reciprocal anchorage.
This is one of the most commonly cited examples in orthodontic biomechanics.

questions.question: 79005. Which appliance is associated with treatment of skeletal Class III due to maxillary deficiency?
questions.explain:
Reverse-pull headgear, or facemask, is used to protract the maxilla.
It is commonly used in growing patients with maxillary deficiency.
It can help correct anterior crossbite associated with skeletal Class III.
Early treatment generally provides greater orthopedic potential.

questions.question: 79004. Which appliance is commonly associated with correction of anterior crossbite caused by a dental problem?
questions.explain:
Z-spring can produce a controlled labial force on a palatally displaced anterior tooth.
It is commonly incorporated into a removable upper appliance.
It is useful for selected dental anterior crossbites.
Adequate space and proper anchorage are necessary for successful correction.

questions.question: 79003. Which appliance is most commonly used for rapid maxillary expansion?
questions.explain:
The Hyrax appliance is a commonly used rapid maxillary expansion (RME) appliance. It applies lateral forces to the maxilla, producing opening/separation of the midpalatal suture in growing patients. This helps correct transverse maxillary deficiency and posterior crossbite.

Hawley retainer: Mainly used for retention after orthodontic treatment.
Twin Block: A functional appliance primarily used for Class II malocclusion with mandibular retrusion.

Frankel: A functional regulator used mainly for dentofacial orthopedic correction.

questions.question: 79002. Maximum anchorage means:
questions.option3: Minimal forward movement of anchorage teeth
questions.explain:
Maximum anchorage means most of the available space is used for movement of the active teeth.
Only a small amount of anchorage-unit movement is permitted.
It is common in extraction cases requiring substantial anterior retraction.
Extraoral appliances or skeletal anchorage may be used for reinforcement.

questions.question: 79001. Headgear is primarily used to modify:
questions.explain:
Maxillary growth/positionExplanation:
Orthodontic headgear can provide extraoral forces to the maxillary dentition and maxilla.
It may be used to restrict forward maxillary growth or distalize maxillary molars.
Its effect depends on the direction and magnitude of force.
It is particularly useful in selected growing Class II patients.

questions.question: 79000. Which cephalometric angle primarily measures the anteroposterior position of the mandible relative to the cranial base?
questions.explain:
The SNB angle indicates the anteroposterior position of the mandible relative to the anterior cranial base.
SNA evaluates the anteroposterior position of the maxilla.
ANB represents the sagittal relationship between the maxilla and mandible.
FMA is primarily related to the vertical skeletal pattern.

questions.question: 78999. Removable appliance is being used to move an incisor labially. The spring should ideally contact the tooth at:
questions.explain: For effective labial tipping of an incisor, the active element is generally positioned appropriately against the lingual surface near the incisal region, depending on the design and desired movement.

questions.question: 78998. Which dental material is most commonly used as a pulp-capping material because of its high pH?
questions.explain:
Calcium hydroxideExplanation:
Calcium hydroxide has a highly alkaline pH.
Its alkalinity provides antibacterial activity and stimulates reparative dentin formation.
It has traditionally been used for direct and indirect pulp capping.
Its major limitation is relatively poor mechanical strength.

questions.question: 78997. Tarnish is best defined as:
questions.option4: Loss of metal due to mechanical wear
questions.explain:
Tarnish is a surface discoloration or alteration of a metal without significant loss of the metal itself.
It usually results from formation of a thin surface film.
It commonly affects metallic dental restorations and appliances.
Tarnish is mainly an aesthetic problem, unlike severe corrosion

questions.question: 78996. A patient presents with a mesial molar relationship and negative overjet. Which diagnosis should be considered first?
questions.explain:
characteristic of Angle Class III.
Mesial molar relationship → mandibular first molar is positioned mesially/anteriorly relative to the maxillary first molar.
Negative overjet → mandibular incisors are positioned ahead of maxillary incisors, producing an anterior crossbite.
Together, these findings are characteristic of Class III malocclusion, which may be skeletal or dental in origin.

questions.question: 78995. A patient has properly aligned teeth, but several teeth are rotated around their long axes. Which of Andrews’ keys is violated?
questions.explain:
One of Andrews’ six keys is absence of rotation, meaning teeth should not be rotated around their long axes.
Molar relationship – Distal marginal ridge of upper 1st molar contacts mesial marginal ridge of lower 2nd molar; MB cusp of upper 1st molar fits in mandibular molar groove.
Crown angulation – Gingival portion of crown is distal to the occlusal portion.
Crown inclination – Correct labiolingual/buccolingual inclination of crowns.
No rotations – Teeth should be free from undesirable rotations.
Tight contacts – No spaces between adjacent teeth.
Curve of Spee – Should be flat or mild (not excessive).

questions.question: 78994. Which combination correctly describes the normal primary dentition?
questions.option1: Crowded anterior teeth + deep overbite + V-shaped arch
questions.option2: Spaced anterior teeth + shallow overbite + ovoid arch
questions.option3: Spaced anterior teeth + deep overbite + narrow arch
questions.option4: Crowded anterior teeth + increased overjet + ovoid arch
questions.explain:
Normal signs of primary dentition :
Spaced anteriors
Primate/anthropoid space
Shallow overjet & over bite
Almost vertical inclination of the anteriors
Ovoid arch form 
Flush/straight terminal plane relation.

questions.question: 78993. Orthognathic surgery should generally be performed:
questions.explain: Orthognathic surgery is generally postponed until skeletal growth is complete to minimize postoperative skeletal changes.

questions.question: 78992. Which statement correctly compares GIC and composite resin?
questions.option1: GIC has better wear resistance than composite
questions.option2: Composite releases fluoride like conventional GIC
questions.option3: GIC chemically bonds to tooth, whereas composite generally requires an adhesive system
questions.option4: Composite is more moisture tolerant during placement
questions.explain: Conventional GIC provides intrinsic chemical adhesion, while composite restorations generally depend on an adhesive bonding system for adhesion to tooth structure.

questions.question: 78991. The ability of a material to absorb energy within its elastic limit is called:
questions.explain:
Resilience represents the energy absorbed during elastic deformation.
The absorbed energy is recoverable when the stress is removed.
It is represented by the area under the stress–strain curve up to the elastic limit.
Toughness, in contrast, includes energy absorbed during both elastic and plastic deformation.

questions.question: 78990. Which wax is primarily used for making the pattern of a casting restoration?
questions.explain: Inlay wax is specifically formulated to produce accurate patterns for cast restorations such as inlays, onlays, and crowns.

questions.question: 78989. Which factor generally increases the setting time of gypsum?
questions.explain:
Decreased water-powder ratio → generally decreases setting time.
Increased spatulation → generally shortens setting time.
Accelerator → decreases setting time.
 Retarder → increases setting time.

questions.question: 78988. Which of the following has the best dimensional stability among elastomeric impression materials?
questions.explain:
Polysulfide: Moderate dimensional stability with some shrinkage.
Condensation silicone: Releases ethyl alcohol as a by-product, causing shrinkage.
 Addition silicone: Excellent dimensional stability because no volatile by-product is produced during polymerization.
 Polyether: Good dimensional stability, but generally less stable than addition silicone.

questions.question: 78987. Which combination is correctly matched?
questions.explain:
Calcium sulfate → Reactor
Sodium phosphate → Retarder
Diatomaceous earth → Filler
Zinc oxide → Filler

questions.question: 78986. Which statement regarding agar impression material is CORRECT?
questions.option2: It is supplied only as a powder
questions.option3: It can be used for full-mouth impressions without deep undercuts
questions.option4: It is mainly used as a bite registration material
questions.explain:
Agar is a reversible hydrocolloid. It changes from sol (fluid) to gel (solid) by cooling and can be converted back to sol by heating. Therefore, its gelation is primarily physical rather than chemical and can be used for full-mouth impressions when deep undercuts are absent.
Alginate → irreversible hydrocolloid
Agar → reversible hydrocolloid

questions.question: 78985. Zinc in amalgam is mainly added because it-
questions.explain:
Zinc has a strong affinity for oxygen.
During manufacturing, it acts as a scavenger/deoxidizer, removing oxygen and preventing oxidation of other alloy constituents.
However, if zinc-containing amalgam is contaminated with moisture during manipulation, it can cause delayed expansion.

questions.question: 78984. A removable appliance is required to close a median diastema using a labial bow. Which design is specifically indicated?
questions.explain:
The split labial bow is mainly used for:
 Retraction of individual incisors
 Correction of anterior spacing
Differential control of anterior teeth
 Retention and stabilization of the anterior segment

questions.question: 78983. Which of the following is NOT a limitation of functional appliances?
questions.option2: Inability to produce individual tooth movement
questions.option3: Inability to use them effectively after growth has ceased
questions.explain: Functional appliances generally do not interfere significantly with oral hygiene maintenance, which is actually listed as an advantage

questions.question: 78982. Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.option3: Mechanical appliance → Active components such as springs and screws
questions.option4: Passive appliance → Elastics producing active tooth movement
questions.explain: Mechanical removable appliances contain springs, elastics, screws, etc., which are activated to produce active force. Passive appliances exert no active pressure.

questions.question: 78981. In Steiner Analysis, what does an increased SNB angle (>80º) indicate?
questions.explain:
SNB angle relates the anteroposterior position of the mandible to the cranial base. 
The average normal anatomical standard value for SNB is 80º. 
A value significantly greater than 80º signifies mandibular prognathism. 
A reduced angle below 80º signifies mandibular retrognathism.

questions.question: 78980. A patient has the mesiobuccal cusp of the maxillary first permanent molar occluding with the anterior buccal groove of the mandibular first permanent molar. Which classification is most appropriate?
questions.explain:
Neutro-occlusion = Angle Class I molar relationship.
In neutro-occlusion, the mesiobuccal cusp of the maxillary first permanent molar occludes with the buccal groove of the mandibular first permanent molar.

questions.question: 78979. Which of the following is an orthopedic effect of a functional appliance?
questions.explain: Functional appliances may accelerate condylar growth, remodel the glenoid fossa, restrict jaw growth or alter the direction of jaw growth.

questions.question: 78978. Which of the following is not listed as a type of malocclusion in the vertical plane in the image?
questions.explain:
Malocclusions on vertical-plane :
Increased/excessive overbite
Reduced overbite
Open bite
Edge-to-edge bite
Posterior crossbite is primarily a transverse-plane malocclusion

questions.question: 78977. What is the primary active function of a Short Labial Bow?
questions.option1: Rapid expansion of the posterior arch
questions.explain:
:Short labial bows contact the labial surface of four upper incisors. 
Closing the vertical U-loops retroclines proclined incisors, reducing overjet. 
It is commonly used as a passive retention element in Hawley retainers. 
It is fabricated using 0.7 mm hard stainless steel wire.

questions.question: 78976. Which malocclusion is a classic indication for an activator?
questions.explain: Class II division 1 is one of the principal indications. Other indications include retrognathic mandible, decreased lower facial height and low mandibular plane angle.

questions.question: 78975. Which is a major limitation of chin-cap therapy?
questions.option1: It cannot be used in growing patients
questions.option2: It has no skeletal effect whatsoever
questions.option3: Its long-term skeletal effect is limited and strongly influenced by growth pattern and compliance
questions.explain: Chin cap may produce favorable changes in selected growing Class III patients, but long-term correction of true mandibular prognathism is unpredictable because mandibular growth continues.

questions.question: 78974. Bite planes are best described as:
questions.explain: A bite plane is a myofunctional appliance, usually incorporated into a removable appliance as an extension or modification of its acrylic base plate.

questions.question: 78973. Which clasp is a modification of the Schwarz arrowhead clasp?
questions.explain: Adams clasp is specifically described as a modification of the Schwarz arrowhead clasp.

questions.question: 78972. What is the primary purpose of incorporating an Upper Anterior Flat Bite Plane?
questions.explain:
Anterior flat bite planes are primarily designed to assist in reducing deep bite. 
Lower incisors contact the flat acrylic, disocclude posterior teeth by 2 to 3 mm. 
Disocclusion allows passive vertical eruption of the posterior teeth. 
It also helps eliminate cuspal interferences during orthodontic movements

questions.question: 78971. Which extraoral device is indicated to restrict the forward and downward growth of a prognathic mandible?
questions.explain:
:A chin cup is an extraoral orthopaedic appliance designed to cover the chin. 
It applies direct force to restrict the downward and forward growth of the mandible. 
It is indicated in Class III malocclusions caused by mild-to-moderate mandibular prognathism.

questions.question: 78970. Which cephalometric finding most strongly indicates a skeletal Class II relationship?
questions.explain: An increased ANB angle generally indicates a skeletal Class II relationship. Approximately 2° is considered a typical Class I relationship, while a negative ANB suggests skeletal Class III.

questions.question: 78969. Anchorage where anchor units are restricted to bodily movement using multiband techniques is called:
questions.explain:
Stationary anchorage refers to designing the anchor unit to move strictly bodily if displaced. 
Bodily movement provides greater resistance to force than simple tipping movement.

questions.question: 78968. All of the following are causes of anchorage loss EXCEPT:
questions.explain: Inadequate wear time, over-activation of springs, and poor appliance retention all directly contribute to unwanted anchor tooth movement and anchorage loss. A transpalatal arch, however, is specifically designed as an anchorage-reinforcing device that connects the molars across the palate to resist unwanted movement. It works by increasing the effective root surface area resisting displacement. So rather than causing anchorage loss, it actively helps prevent it, making it the correct exception here.

questions.question: 78967. Which appliance is specifically noted as tissue-borne when used for retroclination of incisors?
questions.explain: The Frankel appliance is specifically noted as a tissue-borne functional appliance when used for retroclination of incisors, distinguishing it from tooth-borne appliances that rely more directly on dental contact for support and force transmission. The oral screen, while also a functional appliance used for retroclination, is not specifically labeled tissue-borne in this context in the same way. The Johnson twin-wire and Watkin appliances are instead fixed appliance techniques, entirely different in design and support mechanism from a removable, tissue-borne functional appliance. This tissue-borne classification reflects the Frankel appliance's design, which minimizes direct tooth contact in favor of vestibular shields supported by surrounding soft tissue.

questions.question: 78966. What type of anchorage is achieved when two equal and similar groups of teeth move toward each other?
questions.explain:
:Reciprocal anchorage occurs when two equal anchor units exert equal forces on each other.
Both units move equal distances in opposite directions toward or away from each other..

questions.question: 78965. In Steiner's cephalometric analysis, the mean value of the SNA angle is approximately:
questions.explain: Steiner's analysis sets the mean SNA angle at approximately 82°, representing the antero-posterior position of the maxilla relative to the anterior cranial base. A value significantly above this mean indicates a prognathic (forward-positioned) maxilla, while a value below it indicates a retrognathic (set-back) maxilla. This angle is measured from Sella to Nasion to Point A, three standard cephalometric landmarks used across most analyses. It forms one half of the ANB comparison used to classify overall skeletal jaw relationships.

questions.question: 78964. The vestibular screen is chiefly used to intercept:
questions.explain: The vestibular screen is a simple acrylic shield placed in the vestibule, positioned to intercept and correct a mouth breathing habit by encouraging nasal breathing instead. It also provides secondary benefits by helping manage related habits like thumb sucking, tongue thrusting, lip biting, and cheek biting. By acting as a physical barrier, it retrains the perioral musculature over time to adopt more normal function. Bruxism, Class III malocclusion, and TMJ disorders are managed using entirely different clinical approaches unrelated to this simple screen device.

questions.question: 78963. An already-developed (established) anterior crossbite can be treated using a double cantilever spring combined with:
questions.explain: An already-established anterior crossbite can be treated using a double cantilever spring combined with a posterior bite-plane, one of three listed options for this clinical scenario. The posterior bite-plane disengages the bite, allowing the spring to move the crossed-out anterior tooth labially without occlusal interference from the opposing teeth. High-pull headgear, face masks, and chin cups are orthopaedic devices used for entirely different purposes, such as restraining maxillary growth or correcting mandibular prognathism. This combination of an active spring with bite disengagement is a recurring treatment principle for anterior crossbite correction.
